after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
The following table shows the values of a continuous function $f(x)$ over the interval $[4,9].$

| $x$ | $4$ | $5.5$ | $8$ | $9$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $1$ | $4$ | $6$ | $9.5$ |

Use the right Riemann sum, with the three subintervals indicated by the data, to approximate the area under the curve $y=f(x)$ over the interval $[4,9].$
after.worked_solution:
In this case, we have $n=3$ rectangles. Using the right Riemann sum, the area is approximated as 

$$
A≈f(5.5)Δ{x}_{1}+f(8)Δ{x}_{2}+f(9)Δ{x}_{3},
$$

where each $Δ{x}_{i}$ is calculated by considering the step between a particular $x$-value and the previous one, i.e.,

$$
Δ{x}_{i}={x}_{i}-{x}_{i-1}.
$$

We set up a value table that includes the $Δx$'s.

| $x$ | $4$ | $5.5$ | $8$ | $9$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $Δx$ | $-$ | $1.5$ | $2.5$ | $1$ |
| $f(x)$ | $-$ | $4$ | $6$ | $9.5$ |

Finally, we plug in the numbers to approximate the area under the curve and get

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈4\cdot 1.5+6\cdot 2.5+9.5\cdot 1 \\  & =6+15+9.5 \\  & =30.5.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Each subinterval is 5 minutes wide. Using right-endpoint velocities gives 5(25+27+k+18)=450. Thus 70+k=90, so k=20.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
The following table shows the velocity of a plane during a $20$-minute trip.

| $t\,(\text{minutes})$ | $0$ | $5$ | $10$ | $15$ | $20$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $v(t)\,(\text{kilometers/minute})$ | $17$ | $25$ | $27$ | $k$ | $18$ |

If the right Riemann sum approximation of the total distance traveled during this period has a value of  $450\,\text{km}$, what is the value of $k?$

*Hint: The distance traveled is given by the area under the velocity-time graph.*
after.worked_solution:
The area $A$ under the curve $y=v(t)$ can be approximated using the formula

$$
A≈(\overset{\text{heights}}{\overset{⏞}{v(5)+v(10)+v(15)+v(20)}})\cdot {{Δt}_{⏟}}_{\text{width}}.
$$

So, we now set up a table with the values of $v(t)$ at each point:

| $t$ | $5$ | $10$ | $15$ | $20$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $v(t)$ | $25$ | $27$ | $k$ | $18$ |

Now, we obtain the following approximation for the area:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈(25+27+k+18)\cdot 5 \\  & =5(k+70) \\  & =5k+350\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, in the given context, the area under the curve represents the total distance traveled during the $20$ minute period. Since we are given that the right Riemann sum approximation of the total distance is $450\,\text{km},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}5k+350 & =450 \\ 5k & =450-350 \\ k & =\frac{100}{5} \\ k & =20.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: The right endpoints are 2.5, 3, 3.5, and 4, giving heights 25, 16, 9, and 4. The sum is 0.5(25+16+9+4)=27. The function is strictly decreasing on [2,4], so right-endpoint rectangles underestimate the actual area.

after.name: Question 5
after.worked_solution:
Let's sketch our situation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13950940/assets/1cb4c2c69c93117bd5eed39322059a3c0af84d16b293ccfc053c677ac0b6127d.png)

The area $A$ under the graph can be approximated using the formula

$$
A≈(\overset{\text{heights}}{\overset{⏞}{f(2.5)+f(3)+f(3.5)+f(4)}})\cdot {{Δx}_{⏟}}_{\text{width}}.
$$

So, we now set up a table with the values of $f(x)$ at each point:

| $x$ | $2.5$ | $3$ | $3.5$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $25$ | $16$ | $9$ | $4$ |

Finally, we obtain the following approximation for our area:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈(25+16+9+4)\cdot 0.5 \\  & =54\cdot 0.5 \\  & =27\end{aligned}
$$

Because the function is strictly $\text{decreasing}$ over the interval $[2,4],$ the rectangles reach *below* the function, which means our approximation is an $\text{underestimate}$ of the actual area.
